input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages (I think they’re called MMS?) from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and I just can’t get them to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
Yes, it’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002—that’s having the problem with sending picture messages.
I just checked, and it looks like my phone is showing an airplane icon at the top. Does that mean airplane mode is on? Could that be why I can’t send picture messages?
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some bars and a “5G” at the top of my screen, and it says data is enabled. Should I try sending a picture message again now?
I just tried, but it still won’t let me send a picture message. It’s still not working. What should I do next?
I checked, and my phone’s APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not really sure what that means—do those look right, or should I reset something?

I get a bit nervous with these kinds of steps—will resetting the APN or restarting my phone erase any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you please reassure me before I do anything?

Alright, I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to restart my phone now—are you sure that won’t mess up anything else? I just want to double-check before I do it.
My phone has restarted and everything looks the same at the top, but I still can’t send a picture message. It’s getting a bit frustrating—what else can I try?
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I do next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t mention anything about storage or SMS. Should I add those permissions?

Alright, I’ve added both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app. I just tried sending a picture message again, and it looks like it’s working now! Thank you so much for your help—I really appreciate your patience with me.
Thank you so much! I’m relieved it’s working again. I’ll let you know if I have any more trouble, but hopefully everything will stay okay now. Have a great day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you know it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you.

To proceed, could you please confirm which phone number (if you have more than one) is having trouble sending picture messages? If it’s the number you provided (555-123-2002), please let me know, or specify another number if needed.

Thank you for confirming. To help resolve your MMS issue, I’ll guide you through a few steps. First, could you please check if you have cellular service and mobile data enabled on your phone? 

Look at your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- Do you see signal bars (not an “X” or “No Service”)?
- Is there a “4G”, “LTE”, “5G”, or similar icon?
- Is mobile data enabled (not just Wi-Fi)?

This will help determine if the issue is related to your network connection. If you’re unsure, let me know and I can guide you through checking these settings.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I just checked, and it looks like my phone is showing an airplane icon at the top. Does that mean airplane mode is on? Could that be why I can’t send picture messages?

Yes, the airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data—are turned off. This will prevent you from sending or receiving MMS (picture messages).

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to disable Airplane Mode.

Once Airplane Mode is off, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the network. Then, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some bars and a “5G” at the top of my screen, and it says data is enabled. Should I try sending a picture message again now?

Yes, now that Airplane Mode is off and you see signal bars with “5G” and data enabled, please try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if it goes through successfully or if you still experience any issues. If it doesn’t work, I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried, but it still won’t let me send a picture message. It’s still not working. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since you have cellular service and data enabled, the next step is to check if your phone’s MMS settings (APN settings) are correct, as incorrect settings can prevent picture messages from being sent.

Could you please check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings and let me know if you see an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed? If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the process or provide instructions to reset your APN settings to default, which often resolves MMS issues.

Would you like instructions to check or reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked, and my phone’s APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not really sure what that means—do those look right, or should I reset something?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The APN name “internet” and the MMSC URL “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc” appear to be standard, but sometimes issues can still occur even if they look correct.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to default, as this can often resolve hidden configuration issues. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device?

I get a bit nervous with these kinds of steps—will resetting the APN or restarting my phone erase any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you please reassure me before I do anything?

Rest assured, resetting your APN settings and restarting your phone will not erase any of your photos, messages, or personal data. 

Resetting the APN only restores your network settings (like how your phone connects to mobile data and MMS) to their default values. Restarting your phone simply refreshes the system and applies those changes. All your apps, photos, and messages will remain safe and unchanged.

If you’re ready, I can guide you through the steps to reset your APN settings and restart your phone. Let me know if you’d like to proceed or if you have any other questions!

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Restarting your phone after resetting the APN settings is a safe and standard step. It will not affect your photos, messages, apps, or any other personal data. Restarting simply refreshes your phone’s system and ensures the new network settings take effect.

You can go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again. If you have any concerns or run into any issues, I’m here to help!
